verdict: Gartner's reported revenue dipped 1% to $1.50B because it sold a side business — excluding that business, revenue grew 2.4% — and net income leapt to $214M from $35M, when an impairment weighed on the comparison.

segments.name: Insights
segments.note: The core subscription research business — tech and business leaders pay for advice and benchmarks. Its contract value, the future revenue pipeline, reached $5.3B.

segments.name: Conferences
segments.note: Gartner's big symposiums and conferences for executives.

segments.name: Consulting
segments.note: Hands-on consulting engagements built on the research.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: The analysts' support teams, sales force and back office — shown net of a $1M gain on selling a divested operation.

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: Spreading the cost of offices and equipment over their lives.

opex.name: Amortization of intangibles
opex.note: Spreading the cost of past acquisitions over time.

otherDetail: Net interest expense of $24M plus $2M of other expenses.

takeaways.title: The subscription engine accelerated
takeaways.text: Contract value — subscriptions already sold but not yet recognized as revenue — grew 2.5% year over year and 1.1% just in the quarter, its fastest sequential pace in a while.

takeaways.title: EPS comparisons are distorted
takeaways.text: EPS rose 613% partly because last year's quarter absorbed a $150M goodwill impairment, and partly because buybacks shrank the diluted share count from 75.0M to 63.9M.

takeaways.title: Buybacks are doing heavy lifting
takeaways.text: Gartner repurchased $1.7B of its own stock over the last four quarters ($138M this quarter), and raised its full-year guidance for revenue, profit and free cash flow.

oneTimers: The year-ago quarter included a $150M goodwill impairment, which is why profit growth rates look extreme.
Revenue from the divested 'Other' business fell from $55M a year ago to zero; Gartner's adjusted figures exclude it, and on that basis revenue grew 2.4%.
footerNote: Figures are rounded to $M; Insights revenue absorbs a $1M rounding difference so the lines add exactly.
